_about: Source for every demo. Edit this file, then run: python3 tools/build.py. Hotspots are boxes in the raw capture's own pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. 'edits' cover things on a capture that shouldn't show (browser extension icons, test records, wrong logos).

start.headline: A parent asks about your school at 9:47 PM.
start.body: Your office closed hours ago. Here's what Banner Connect does next, without anyone on your staff lifting a finger.

steps.title: A parent reaches out after hours
steps.body: Sarah is on your website after her kids are in bed. She asks about 2nd grade for her son, Mateo, and how admissions works.
steps.alt: Banner Christian School's Request Info Packet form, filled in by Sarah Ramirez for 2nd grade

steps.title: Her info packet arrives right away
steps.body: The first email goes out the moment she submits. Your school's name and her first name fill in on their own, so it reads like it came from your office.
steps.alt: The first nurture email: subject line with the school's name and a thank-you note with a link to the info packet

steps.title: She lands in your enrollment pipeline
steps.body: Every family who reaches out shows up in New Inquiry, with where they found you and how long since anyone talked to them.
steps.alt: The Inquiry to Enrollment pipeline with the Ramirez Family in the New Inquiry column

steps.title: Your team knows who to call
steps.body: Follow-ups land on your admissions director's task list. Anything past due turns red, so no family slips through the cracks.
steps.alt: The dashboard task list with follow-up calls assigned to the admissions director

steps.title: One workflow does all of it
steps.body: Behind the scenes, one automation creates the pipeline card, tags the family, and sends three emails over ten days. Banner 61 sets it up for you.
steps.alt: The Request Info Packet workflow: form trigger, create opportunity, add tag, then three emails with waits between them

finish.headline: One inquiry, handled while your office was closed.
finish.body: Every family hears back right away, and your team always knows the next step.

start.headline: Most families need more than one email before they visit.
start.body: Here's how Banner Connect keeps the conversation going for ten days, so your staff doesn't have to remember to.

steps.title: Three emails, spaced out on purpose
steps.body: Day 1 sends the info packet. Day 3 explains what makes your school different. Day 10 invites the family to take the next step.
steps.alt: The nurture workflow with three emails separated by 3-day and 7-day waits

steps.title: Day 3: why your school
steps.body: This one speaks to what parents are really asking: will my child be ready for life, not just tests? It covers faith-integrated learning, character and academics.
steps.alt: Nurture email #2 explaining holistic learning, character development and faith-integrated curriculum

steps.title: Day 10: an easy next step
steps.body: The last email offers three clear paths: schedule a visit, explore financial aid, or start an application. Each one is a single click.
steps.alt: Nurture email #3 with links to schedule a visit, learn about financial aid and apply

steps.title: Every email is a template you can edit
steps.body: Change the wording once and every family gets the new version. Your school's name, address and phone fill in automatically.
steps.alt: The email template library in grid view

steps.title: A sequence for every kind of inquiry
steps.body: Tuition questions, financial aid, visits, events and families who went quiet each get their own follow-up, already built and ready to turn on.
steps.alt: The Prebuilt Workflows folder listing seven admissions automations

finish.headline: Ten days of thoughtful follow-up, and nobody had to hit send.
finish.body: Your team steps in when a family is ready to talk. The emails handle the rest.

start.headline: The visit is where families decide.
start.body: Here's how a parent books a campus visit on their own, and how Banner Connect makes sure they actually show up.

steps.title: Parents pick a day that works
steps.body: Your booking page shows only the times you're available. No back-and-forth emails to find a slot.
steps.alt: The Schedule a Visit booking page with November dates available

steps.title: Then a time
steps.body: Sarah picks 10:00 AM on Thursday. The visit is blocked on your calendar the moment she confirms.
steps.alt: The booking page with 10:00 AM on Thursday, November 5 selected

steps.title: A few details and she's booked
steps.body: She adds a note for your team. It goes straight onto her record, so whoever gives the tour knows what to expect.
steps.alt: The booking details form filled in by Sarah Ramirez with a note about her son starting 2nd grade

steps.title: Reminders go out on their own
steps.body: A confirmation right away, a reminder the day before, and another an hour before. Fewer families forget.
steps.alt: The Request a Visit workflow: confirmation email, then reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before the visit

steps.title: After the visit, one click from your team
steps.body: Your staff marks how it went. Attended moves the family forward. A no-show gets a friendly reschedule email automatically.
steps.alt: The workflow branches for visit attended, no-show with reschedule email, and not a fit

finish.headline: Booked, reminded and followed up, all without a phone call.
finish.body: Your team spends its time on the visit itself, not on scheduling it.

start.headline: Where is every family in your admissions process?
start.body: With Banner Connect, the answer is one screen away.

steps.title: Every stage, from inquiry to enrolled
steps.body: Families move left to right: New Inquiry, Visit Scheduled, Visit Attended, Application Sent and on to enrolled. Each column shows how many families and how much tuition.
steps.alt: The pipeline columns with family counts and tuition totals

steps.title: Every family has a card
steps.body: See where they came from, what they're worth in tuition and how many days since your last contact. Cards tagged Cold need attention.
steps.alt: A family card showing lead source, tuition value and days since last contact

steps.title: And a to-do list that keeps up
steps.body: Follow-ups are assigned to a person with a due date. Overdue calls turn red so they get handled first.
steps.alt: The task list with overdue follow-ups assigned to the admissions director

finish.headline: No more spreadsheets or sticky notes.
finish.body: Everyone on your team sees the same picture of every family.

start.headline: Some families go quiet. That doesn't mean they've said no.
start.body: Here's how Banner Connect checks back in with families who stopped responding.

steps.title: A family goes cold
steps.body: The Johnson Family asked about your school, then nothing. After a stretch with no contact, their card gets a Cold tag.
steps.alt: A pipeline card for the Johnson Family with a Cold tag

steps.title: Four check-ins over two weeks
steps.body: The Cold tag starts a short series: four emails spaced 3, 4 and 7 days apart. If the family replies, your team takes it from there.
steps.alt: The Cold Inquiry Revival workflow with four emails and waits between them

steps.title: Short, personal and easy to answer
steps.body: "Still thinking about our school?" It's signed by your admissions director and asks one simple question. Parents just hit reply.
steps.alt: Cold Inquiry Revival email #1 with the subject Still thinking about the school

finish.headline: Families who went quiet get a second chance.
finish.body: And your team doesn't have to remember who to chase.

start.headline: How is enrollment really going?
start.body: Your dashboard answers that before your board asks.

steps.title: See where families drop off
steps.body: The funnel shows how many families reach each stage, and what share move on to the next. You can spot the stage that needs work.
steps.alt: The enrollment funnel from New Inquiry through Enrolled with conversion percentages

steps.title: Tuition and families in the pipeline
steps.body: Two numbers every head of school wants: how much tuition is in play, and how many families are in it.
steps.alt: Dashboard tiles showing $416.5K tuition in pipeline and 46 families

steps.title: Open, won and lost at a glance
steps.body: See how many families are still deciding, how many enrolled and how many chose elsewhere.
steps.alt: Chart of all families by status: open, won and lost

finish.headline: Real numbers, always up to date.
finish.body: No more pulling reports together the night before a board meeting.
